claim: L10 (LFP-primary analysis spec): MI between area x layer node band-power trial vectors as a model-free complement to L7 (correlation) and L9 (Granger/PSI), reported as a convergence check not an independent result, plus an agreement statistic vs L7's correlation matrices.
implementation: context/figures/L10_mutual_information_convergence/L10_mutual_information_convergence.py. Imports sessions_with_nodes, node_trial_traces, correlation_matrix DIRECTLY from L7_cross_area_power_correlation.py -- MI is computed on the exact same per-trial band-power vectors L7 already correlates, not a re-derived version, so the two statistics are genuinely comparable on identical inputs. sklearn.feature_selection.mutual_info_regression (k-NN continuous estimator), both directions computed per pair, matrix entry is their mean. Agreement statistic: Spearman rho between flattened upper-triangle MI and |Pearson r|, per session/band/condition.
self_test: (a) linear synthetic pair (r=0.78) -> MI=0.504 nats -- sanity PASS. (b) NONLINEAR pair (Y=(X-mean)^2+noise, r=-0.11 by construction) -> MI=1.097 nats, clearly above independent baseline (0.004 nats) -- PASS, demonstrates MI catches real dependence Pearson r misses, exactly the spec's 'model-free complement' framing. (c) agreement statistic recovers Spearman rho=0.61 (p=0.017) on pairs with smoothly varying linear-dependence strength -- PASS. (d) determinism check PASS.

real_run.runtime: 4m47s (3 sessions x 5 bands x 2 conditions x up to 15 node pairs each, MI computed both directions per pair)
real_run.finding: Agreement between MI and |Pearson r| is consistently and strongly POSITIVE across all 30 session x band x condition combinations (Spearman rho range 0.32-0.95, every single one positive, median ~0.8). sub-V182o_ses-260629 (the sparsest-coupling session per L7's own finding) shows the weakest agreement (0.32-0.79); sub-V182o_ses-260702 and sub-V182o_ses-260715 (denser coupling per L7) show strong tight agreement (0.66-0.95).
real_run.interpretation_stated_as_descriptive: MI and Pearson correlation rank node pairs similarly across this corpus's band-power structure -- no evidence of nonlinear dependence Pearson r would be missing. Per spec's own framing this is read as corroborating L7's correlation-based ranking, not as an independent finding about which pairs are truly coupled -- stated explicitly in the README, matching the spec's own 'report as a convergence check, not an independent result' instruction.

not_yet_done: MI computed on the same single-representative-channel-per-node vectors L7/L8/L9 all use (inherited limitation, not rebuilt here). No FDR-style multiplicity correction applied to the agreement statistic across the 30 session x band x condition combinations -- reported as 30 individual descriptive numbers, consistent with the spec's own non-inferential framing for this item ('convergence check', not a formal test).
